Elena,

Thanks for the clear ask — glad Nimbus is considering a longer-term partnership. High level plan attached: we can support 24-36 month terms with a staged-commit ladder and a short canary for any capacity/model variant changes.

Highlights here: 
- Staged ramp: quarterly buckets (Q1: 30% baseline, Q2: +30%, Q3: +20%, Q4: +20%) with a 10% runway buffer on each quarter; true-ups at quarter close.
- Canary: 4-week canary on a mirrored pool (zero blast radius to prod) + automated rollback to previous model/variant on regressions.
- Pricing: blended committed rate for the first 12 months with an annual step-down at pre-agreed thresholds; overages billed monthly.
- Auto-renew: default opt-in, with a 60-day notice to opt-out and one-time early-exit clause (pro-rated credit if exit triggered before 12 months).

Ill loop in Karthik for the pricing worksheet and Marissa for contractual language. Attached: redwood-commit-summary-v2.xlsx (workbook with tiered examples) and a draft SOW.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik to confirm pricing figures and costs for canary pools
2) Internal legal + Marissa to prepare redlines to SOW
3) Procurement questionnaire returned by Nimbus this Friday so legal can review
4) Target signature window: 2027-07-15 to 2027-07-30 (DocuSign link once SOW agreed)

Would you like a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the phased numbers?

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Camila team,

Attached is the populated workbook (redwood-commit-summary-v2.xlsx) with three scenarios: 24M conservative, 24M aggressive, 36M phased. Notes:
- Canary pool pricing is modeled as a reserved micro-pool billed at 60% of standard dedicated unit; actual per-token cost during canary will depend on model variant.
- For quarterly true-ups we proposed a smoothing mechanism: 50% of overage billed immediately, 50% credited against next quarter if usage normalizes (this reduces surprise spikes).
- Early-exit: suggested pro-rated credit equal to unused committed value minus one quarters minimum usage floor. This preserves economic symmetry for Redwood.

I also added an operational appendix for canary rollback triggers (latency > 30% baseline, error rate > 2x baseline, quality regression flagged by eval set). Neha, confirm whether these triggers are operationally reasonable.

Marissa, Im OK with the auto-renew 60-day opt-out but recommend adding a contractual notice requirement for price changes during renewal.

Karthik
